tagline.text: The ruins of the 1596 San Jacinto church on the Cagayan River and its old bell

location.label: Location
location.text: Poblacion (Centro), Camalaniugan, Cagayan, on the west bank of the Cagayan River

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200~800 (day-trip transport from Tuguegarao; admission to be confirmed separately)

children.text: These are the ruins of the old Church of San Jacinto de Polonia beside the Cagayan River, declared a National Historical Landmark in 1939. The belfry of the new church next door holds a bell said to have been cast in 1595, and an old brick kiln still stands by the river.

Camalaniugan is a small town in northern Cagayan, on the stretch where the Cagayan River nears the sea. It is said that Spanish Dominican missionaries founded the town on June 15, 1596, and made Saint Hyacinth of Poland (San Jacinto de Polonia in Spanish) its patron saint. Today a new church built in the 1990s stands in the middle of town, and just behind it, on the riverbank, lie the brick walls of the old church. These are the Camalaniugan Church Ruins covered in this guide.

The old church is said to have begun as a modest building with a thatched roof. From the 17th to the 19th century it endured earthquakes, floods, fires and typhoons, and was repaired again and again. Some sources say it was rebuilt in 1746 after a fire in 1719, while others say it suffered typhoons and floods after the 1845 earthquake. In 1898 a typhoon blew off the roof, and because the wall was crumbling toward the river, it was not repaired; instead a new church was planned farther from the river. That is how the ruins came to be. Dates and events differ from source to source, so it is worth comparing them with the on-site signs or what church staff tell you.

The National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) declared the site a National Historical Landmark in 1939. It is not a grand cathedral, but its appeal is that brick structures from the era when the Cagayan Valley was a center of Spanish missionary work stand exposed to the elements just as they are. From the ruins the Cagayan River looks wide and slow, and at sunset the sky glows red above the rice fields and coconut palms across the water. There are few visitors, so it is a good place to walk and take photos in peace.

The brick belfry beside the new church holds the Santa Maria bell, said to have been cast in 1595. The inscription is reported as "Santa Maria de Binalatoca," and a widely told account says it was brought from Binalatongan in Pangasinan (now San Carlos City). Other accounts say its origin is uncertain, so it is hard to be definitive. It is often presented as the oldest bell in the Philippines, or in the Far East. About 1 km from town along the river stands the kiln (horno) that fired bricks for churches and public buildings. It is estimated to date from the 18th century, and the view of the town and river from the top is said to be wonderful. Walking slowly, you can see the church ruins, the belfry and the kiln in 1 to 2 hours, which makes this a good stop in the middle of a day trip around the old churches of Cagayan. Access may vary with local conditions, so it helps to ask the town tourism office or the parish office before you go.

blocks.title: Old church walls on the riverbank

children.text: Right behind the new church, old brick walls stand on the bank of the Cagayan River. There is no roof, and the tops of the walls have worn low in many places, so the traces of time are plain to see. On the river side you can see protection works built to keep the bank from collapsing.

The NHCP declared it a National Historical Landmark in 1939. Find the marker and read its text, then compare it with what you see; it makes the history much easier to follow. Check the wording and dates on the marker yourself on site.

Hanging in the new brick belfry, this bell is presented as the oldest in the Philippines. The inscription and decoration on its surface are striking, and other Spanish-era bells are said to hang with it. It is safest to ask at the parish office whether the belfry is open.

The present church connected to the old site was built in the 1990s. Its facade is neat, and if you come at Mass time you can glimpse the daily life of local parishioners. Please stay quiet during Mass and refrain from taking photos.

This kiln, about 1 km from the church along the river, is estimated to date from the 18th century. It is said to have fired bricks for churches, bridges and government buildings across Cagayan. The 360-degree view from the top is great, but check the condition of the stairs yourself before climbing.

Beside the ruins you can see the lower reaches of the Cagayan River, the longest river in the Philippines. The river is wide, which makes it good for sunset photos, and small boats occasionally pass by.

blocks.title: A stop on the Cagayan church tour

children.text: It often appears on Visita Iglesia (church tour) routes that link the old churches of Cagayan, such as Lal-lo. It is a rewarding stop not only for Catholics but also for travelers interested in architecture and history.

items.title: Half-day route staying in Aparri
items.subtitle: Taking your time around the church ruins and the kiln

children.text: Take a jeepney or van from Aparri toward Camalaniugan. Tell the driver you want to get off at the town church (Centro church).
Arrive in front of the new church, admire the facade, and go inside if there is no Mass.
Walk to the back of the church to see the old church walls and the marker. Go to the riverside bank and enjoy the view.
Look at the 1595 bell in the brick belfry, and ask the parish office whether it is open.
Take a tricycle or walk to the brick kiln and look around.
Have lunch at a restaurant in town and head to your next destination.
There is almost no shade at midday and it is very hot. If possible, visit early in the morning or late in the afternoon.

items.title: Full-day Cagayan church route
items.subtitle: From Tuguegarao, touring the old churches to the north

children.text: Take a bus or van from Tuguegarao toward Aparri. Check the departure time at the terminal.
Get off at Camalaniugan and look around the church ruins, the belfry and the kiln.
Have lunch in town.
Move on to nearby old churches and sites such as Lal-lo. Check the means of transport locally.
Check the return transport before sunset and head back to Tuguegarao or Aparri.
The last ride back may leave early, so be sure to confirm the return time in advance.
There are flights from Manila (NAIA) to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG). Check the airline's announcements for operation and schedules.

10–12 hours

Tuguegarao is the hub for travel in Cagayan. See also the registered Tuguegarao entry.
Camalaniugan is about
94 km
north of Tuguegarao.
From Tuguegarao, take a bus, van or jeepney toward Aparri or Camalaniugan and get off at the town entrance. Check fares and schedules locally.
Camalaniugan lies on the route between Lal-lo and Aparri, so you use the same line whichever way you come from.
A jeepney heading south from Aparri gets you close. Ask the driver to let you off at the town church.
If the church is some distance from where you get off on the main road, take a tricycle. One 2018 travel account says it cost

Cagayan is affected by the northeast monsoon and typhoons. Since this is a trip on foot around outdoor ruins, November to April, when there is less rain and the river is calmer, is the safe choice. Some winter days can be cloudy under the northeast wind, so check the forecast.
The Cagayan River can swell greatly in the rainy season. The site is close to the riverbank, so postpone your visit if there is a typhoon or heavy rain warning.

Within the day, 8 to 10 a.m. and after 4 p.m. are best. The light is soft then, the color of the bricks shows well, and the sunset spreading over the river is beautiful. Sunday Mass times in the town church bring more people, so choose a weekday if you want quiet.

Camalaniugan is small and has few lodgings for travelers. Most visitors stay in nearby Aparri, Tuguegarao or the Lal-lo area and come as a day trip. Aparri is a port city where the Cagayan River meets the sea, with a fairly varied choice of lodging and restaurants. Tuguegarao has the most options. Check booking sites for the latest accommodation information.

You can eat simply at small eateries (carinderias) in town. Fish dishes are common in Cagayan because the river and the sea are close, and pancit batil patung is famous around Tuguegarao. It helps to bring a packed lunch or snacks from Tuguegarao or Aparri before you visit. When arranging lodging, asking the Cagayan provincial tourism office or lodgings in Aparri can also get you transport information.
Midday sun is strong, so be sure to bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
The ruined walls are old and may be weak, so do not climb or lean on them.
Stay quiet during Mass and refrain from taking photos. Modest clothing is best inside the church.
If you want to see the belfry and bell up close, first ask the parish office whether it is open.
The last ride back may leave early, so check the time in advance.
Combining it with nearby old churches such as Lal-lo makes a rewarding day trip.
When taking photos, do not stand too close to the edge of the riverbank.
Cash is widely used in town, so bring plenty of small bills.
The ruins stand on a riverbank under threat from erosion, so do not go near the edge or climb the walls, and avoid visiting during typhoons or heavy rain.
Admission fees, opening hours and whether the belfry is open were not confirmed in public sources. Check locally.
Years and events differ from source to source, so it is best to compare them with on-site signs.
Bus, van and jeepney fares and schedules change often. Check the latest information locally.
There is little shade and a risk of heatstroke, so avoid midday visits and drink plenty of water.
Refrain from entering the church interior and taking photos during Mass or funerals.
The central city of Cagayan, about
2 hours
south by road. It has the best lodging, restaurants and transport links.
A historic town in the lower Cagayan River area where tours of the nearby old churches are common. Check how to get there locally.
A port city where the Cagayan River meets the sea, good as a base for lodging. You can get there by jeepney.
A signature natural attraction of Cagayan that many people include in a Cagayan itinerary.
